name: ADT plus DOCEtaxel (metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer)

biomarkers.note: Cytotoxic intensification is not biomarker-restricted; ADT is the required castration backbone. Docetaxel intensification is most established for high-volume synchronous metastatic castration-sensitive disease. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Prostate Cancer, Principles of ADT for mCSPC (PROS-G) and Discussion.

lineOfTherapy: first-line systemic treatment intensification for metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (ADT plus docetaxel); an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor is commonly added as triplet therapy in fit patients

eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, PROS-G (ADT for Patients with mCSPC), prostate lines 2957 to 2961 (ADT plus docetaxel and an ARPI)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: fit for taxane chemotherapy (adequate organ and marrow function, acceptable performance status)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, Discussion (triplet therapy fit for chemotherapy), prostate line 536

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: concurrent ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL (orchiectomy, LHRH agonist, or LHRH antagonist)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, PROS-G footnote h, prostate line ~2999

drugs.name: DOCEtaxel

provenance.locator: Discussion, prostate line 6889 (docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks x 6 doses plus ADT); prostate line 6901 (confirmed survival advantage of adding docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 Discussion, prostate line 6889 (docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks x 6 doses plus ADT). ISMP tall-man DOCEtaxel. 75 mg/m2 IV on day 1 of a 21-day cycle, for 6 cycles. In the mCSPC (castration-sensitive) doublet setting docetaxel is given WITHOUT prednisone.

premedications.name: Corticosteroid premedication for docetaxel (fluid retention / hypersensitivity)
premedications.notes: Give per docetaxel labeling (dexamethasone premedication); specific premedication schedule not enumerated in the provided prostate extract.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Provide per emetogenic-risk tier on the day of chemotherapy.

supportiveCare: continue ADT (LHRH agonist/antagonist or orchiectomy) throughout to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL (PROS-G footnote h).

an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (abiraterone, apalutamide, darolutamide, or enzalutamide) is added as triplet therapy in fit patients per PROS-G (prostate lines 2957 to 2961); see gu-prostate-adt-arpi for ARPI dosing.
G-CSF: assess febrile-neutropenia risk per taxane chemotherapy standards.
monitor for peripheral neuropathy, fluid retention, and hypersensitivity (docetaxel).

monitoring: peripheral neuropathy assessment before each cycle
PSA and serum testosterone (confirm castrate level)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 neutropenia or febrile neutropenia
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and dose-reduce docetaxel per labeling; consider G-CSF prophylaxis; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: docetaxel added to ADT improves survival in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (CHAARTED/STAMPEDE-era evidence)

guideline.locator: PROS-G (ADT for mCSPC with treatment intensification), prostate lines 2957 to 2961; Discussion, docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks x 6 doses (prostate lines 6889, 6901)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for ADT plus DOCEtaxel in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (disease #53 mCSPC). The docetaxel dose (75 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks for 6 doses/cycles, given with ADT and without prednisone in the castration-sensitive doublet) is dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 Discussion (prostate lines 6889 and 6901). ADT is the required castration backbone (PROS-G footnote h). Triplet therapy adds an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor for fit patients (see gu-prostate-adt-arpi). cycleLengthDays 21 and cycles 6 are source-stated (every 3 weeks x 6 doses). No dose was invented or inferred. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
